title: Topoi & Sheaves — Where Geometry Meets Logic
category_reason: A seven-part interactive journey through Grothendieck's sheaf theory and topos theory: presheaves, gluing, Grothendieck topologies, sites, topoi, and internal intuitionistic logic. Pure algebraic geometry / category theory / mathematical logic with no AI or ML content.
thesis: A seven-section interactive English-language journey through Grothendieck's sheaf theory and topos theory, from presheaves on open sets through the gluing axiom, Grothendieck topologies on arbitrary categories, sites, the topos as a universe of sets twisted by geometry, to internal intuitionistic logic where truth values become open sets and the law of excluded middle can fail.
key_claims: A presheaf is a contravariant functor F: O(X)^op → Set assigning data to open sets with restriction maps; the 'contravariant' flip means inclusions U→V induce restrictions F(V)→F(U).
A sheaf is a presheaf satisfying two axioms for every covering: locality (sections agreeing on a cover are equal) and gluing (compatible local sections produce a unique global section).

Grothendieck topologies generalize the notion of covering from topological spaces to arbitrary categories: a rule declaring which families of arrows count as 'coverings' determines what 'local' means.
A Grothendieck topos is a category equivalent to Sh(C,J) for some site (C,J); it has products, coproducts, exponentials, a subobject classifier Ω, and internal logic.
In the topos Sh(X) of sheaves on a space X, truth values are open sets of X: a proposition can be 'true on U' and 'false on V', making logic local and intuitionistic (excluded middle can fail).
Sheafification is the left adjoint to the inclusion Sh(C,J) ↪ [C^op, Set], making every Grothendieck topos a left-exact reflective subcategory of a presheaf topos.

internal_tensions: The page mentions étale, fppf, and Zariski topologies as examples of Grothendieck topologies on algebraic objects but never develops them, creating a gap between the elementary sheaf intuition built in sections 1–3 and the advanced algebraic-geometric applications referenced in sections 4–5.

The meaningful sliver has structure: clusters (frequent phrasing, idiom), filaments (productive grammar connecting clusters), and voids (ungrammatical or never-uttered sequences).

Language is scale-invariant: clusters, filaments, and voids appear at every level from discourse to token; there is no preferred scale.
Metaphor is a long-range filament connecting distant regions of meaning space, not a short step within a cluster.
Paraphrase = moving inside a fiber of the form→meaning map π; synonymy is a property of fibers, not of individual words.
Compositionality is the commutative diagram π'∘f = g∘π: transforming form then interpreting equals interpreting then transforming meaning.

thesis: A seven-section German interactive essay that builds from sheaf theory (presheaves on sin(x), gluing conditions) through ∞-sheaves (gluing up to homotopy) and HoTT (types as spaces, embedding spaces in AI) to an epistemological claim — the world is a sheaf of traces observed through multiple channels — and finally to AI: the loss function is an energy landscape, the model finds the best gluing of training data, and hallucination occurs when it glues where no coherent training sections exist.
key_claims: A presheaf F: Open(X)^op → Set assigns local data with restriction maps; the gluing condition (compatible local sections → unique global section) makes it a sheaf.

∞-sheaves replace strict equality on overlaps with isomorphisms: sᵢ|ᵢⱼ ≅ sⱼ|ᵢⱼ, with the isomorphisms themselves satisfying higher coherence conditions — 'equality becomes a structure, not a property.'

Epistemology: a world event w produces traces e = f(w) through multiple channels fᵢ (eyes, ears, instruments, testimony); a world model is 'true' when its local sections glue coherently, at least up to homotopy.
Science is the art of isolating contact points between model and world — experiments with few free variables where gluing can be tested.
A language model's loss is an energy landscape: θ* = argmin E[L(f_θ(x), y)]; the model lands in a valley representing the best gluing of all training traces.

Hallucination is a gluing where no gluing should exist: when the model encounters a context where local training sections do not coherently overlap, it interpolates — producing plausible-sounding but false output.
Local minima in the loss landscape correspond to consistent but incomplete world models.

title: Ricci-Fluss – Visuelle Erklärung
category_reason: A German-language interactive visual explanation of the Ricci flow as a geometric evolution equation: what it is, the heat-equation analogy, curve-smoothing demos, curvature visualization, and its role in Perelman's proof of the Poincaré conjecture. Pure differential geometry / geometric analysis with no AI or ML content.
thesis: A German-language interactive visual explanation of the Ricci flow (∂g/∂t = −2Rᵢⱼ): what it is, how it works (heat-equation analogy for curvature), three canvas demos (2D curve smoothing, surface deformation, curvature coloring), the step-by-step algorithm, singularity analysis, and its role in Hamilton's 1982 program and Perelman's 2003 proof of the Poincaré conjecture.
key_claims: The Ricci flow deforms a Riemannian metric proportionally to the Ricci curvature: regions of positive curvature shrink, regions of negative curvature expand, flattening the geometry over time.
It is analogous to the heat equation but acting on curvature instead of temperature: an unevenly heated metal plate evens out, and the Ricci flow 'evens out' the shape of a space.
Richard Hamilton introduced the flow in 1982; Grigori Perelman used it (with topological surgery at singularities) to prove the Poincaré conjecture in 2003.
In 2D, the analogous flow (curve shortening) smooths any closed curve to a circle — the Ricci flow is the higher-dimensional generalization toward the sphere.
Singularities (where curvature blows up in finite time) are the main obstruction to global convergence; Perelman's key contribution was the surgery procedure that removes them.
The flow converges (after surgery) to a geometry of constant positive curvature, implying the manifold is a sphere (Poincaré).

internal_tensions: The file presents the Ricci flow as converging to constant curvature in the 'ideal case' but the actual theorem requires surgery at singularities; the visual demos only show the smooth convergence case, potentially misleading about the mathematical difficulty of Perelman's proof.

title: Daniel Paul Schreber – Denkwürdigkeiten eines Nervenkranken
category_reason: A German-language interactive exploration of Daniel Paul Schreber's 1903 psychiatric memoir and its interpretations by Freud, Lacan, and Foucault. Pure psychiatry / literary history / philosophy of mind with no AI or ML content.
thesis: A German-language interactive exploration of Daniel Paul Schreber's 1903 memoir 'Denkwürdigkeiten eines Nervenkranken': his life as a senior Saxon judge, his 1884 psychotic breakdown, the elaborate theological delusional system he constructed (God as omnipotent torturer, women as seals of damnation, his own mission to save humanity), and the subsequent interpretations by Freud (structural paranoia), Lacan (foreclosure of the Name-of-the-Father), and Foucault (madness as social production).
key_claims: Daniel Paul Schreber (1842–1937) was a senior judge in the Saxony court who suffered a psychotic break in 1884 after a period of severe overwork and exhaustion.

He constructed an elaborate delusional theology: God communicated with him directly through 'nerves' and 'rays,' women were 'seals of damnation' placed by God to tempt him, and he was ultimately appointed to save the human race from divine abuse.
Freud (1911) analyzed the case as structural paranoia rooted in castration anxiety and the turn of passive into active homosexual object choice.

Lacan used the Schreber case to develop the concept of the 'foreclosure of the Name-of-the-Father' (forclusion du Nom-du-Père): the fundamental signifier is rejected from the symbolic order, producing psychosis rather than neurosis.
Foucault cited Schreber in 'Madness and Civilization' as an example of how modern society produces madness through exclusion: the 'insane' are defined by their removal from the rational social order.
The memoir is now considered a landmark of both psychiatric literature and modernist literary theory (its fragmented, self-contradicting narrative anticipates stream-of-consciousness fiction).
visualizations: tabbed sections (biography, delusional system, Freud, Lacan, Foucault, legacy)

internal_tensions: The file presents three conflicting interpretations (Freud's psychoanalytic, Lacan's structuralist, Foucault's socio-historical) side by side without adjudicating between them — appropriate for a historical overview, but a casual reader may be left unsure which reading is authoritative.

title: ROME – Fakten in GPT lokalisieren und editieren
category_reason: A German-language interactive walkthrough of the ROME paper (Meng, Bau, Andonian & Belinkov 2022): locating factual associations in GPT via causal tracing (indirect effects on hidden states) and editing them with a single rank-one MLP weight update. Core transformer interpretability and model editing.
thesis: A German-language interactive walkthrough of the ROME paper (Meng, Bau, Andonian & Belinkov 2022): how to locate where GPT stores factual associations (via causal tracing — measuring indirect effects on hidden states across the layer/token grid) and how to edit them with a single rank-one weight update to an MLP layer, replacing a fact (e.g., 'Space Needle is in Seattle' → 'Paris') without destroying the rest of the model.
key_claims: A transformer's hidden states h(l,i) form a grid indexed by layer l and token position i; each cell combines an attention contribution (looking at earlier tokens) and an MLP contribution (local computation).

Causal tracing measures the indirect effect of a hidden state: corrupt the input, then patch only state h(l,i) to its clean value; the recovery of P(target token) measures how much information flows through that state.
Causal tracing identifies two 'bright zones': the 'early site' (middle layers at the last subject token, primarily in the MLP) and the 'late site' (last layers at the last token).
Factual knowledge is stored primarily in MLP layers, not attention layers — the MLP acts as a key-value memory.
ROME (Rank-One Model Editing): a single rank-one update to one MLP weight matrix W₂ can replace a fact while preserving performance on all other facts.
The edit is computed as a closed-form solution to a constrained optimization: minimize the change to the weight matrix subject to the model producing the new answer for the target fact.

title: Wie NNs beliebige Muster bauen – Mechanismen-Visualisierung
category_reason: A German-language interactive visualization explaining how neural networks build arbitrary patterns: the universal approximation theorem, local-expert hidden units, gradient descent training, and hierarchical feature learning in deep networks. Core neural-network theory and mechanism explanation.
thesis: A German-language interactive visualization explaining how neural networks build arbitrary patterns: from the universal approximation theorem (one hidden layer suffices in principle) through the mechanism of how individual hidden units learn to be local experts, to the full training process (gradient descent on a loss landscape) and hierarchical feature learning in deep networks.
key_claims: The universal approximation theorem: a single hidden layer with sufficiently many units and a non-polynomial activation function can approximate any continuous function on a compact set to arbitrary precision.
In practice, hidden units learn to be 'local experts': each unit fires strongly in a region of input space and weakly elsewhere, and the network output is a weighted sum of these local contributions.

Training via gradient descent adjusts weights so that each unit's contribution becomes increasingly aligned with the target function; the loss landscape is non-convex but gradient methods work in practice.
Deeper networks learn hierarchical features: lower layers detect local patterns (edges, parts), and higher layers compose them into global structures (wholes, categories).
The 'mechanism' of approximation is not a single clever trick but the collective contribution of many simple local experts whose weighted sum produces the global function.

key_claims: The pullback of f: X → Z and g: Y → Z is the object P = {(x,y) ∈ X×Y | f(x) = g(y)} with projection maps p₁: P → X and p₂: P → Y satisfying f∘p₁ = g∘p₂.

In topology, pulling back a continuous function along a continuous map gives the composite function on the product space.

thesis: A six-section interactive Plotly-based English-language explorer of Homotopy Type Theory: types as spaces (Bool, ℕ, S¹, ⊥), equality as paths (multiple proofs between the same endpoints), homotopy as continuous deformation of paths, higher paths on a 3D sphere (the ∞-groupoid tower), the univalence axiom (equivalent types are equal), and a 'Rosetta Stone' network graph showing how concepts from topology, logic, and type theory become one and the same in HoTT.
key_claims: In HoTT, every type is a space and every term is a point in that space; Bool has two points (true, false), ℕ is a countably infinite discrete space, S¹ has a base point and a non-trivial loop, and ⊥ is empty.
A proof of a = b is a path from a to b; different proofs are different paths, and the space of equalities between two points can be rich and interesting.
A homotopy is a continuous deformation of one path into another — a 'path between paths' — representing an equality between equalities.
The tower of higher paths (points → paths → homotopies → homotopies between homotopies → …) makes types into ∞-groupoids.
The univalence axiom: if two types are equivalent (there is a perfect two-way mapping with coherence), they are equal; A ≃ B implies A = B. Structure-preserving equivalence is identity.

HoTT unifies three fields: topology (spaces, points, paths, homotopies, homeomorphisms), logic (propositions, proofs, equality proofs, logical equivalence), and type theory (types, terms, identity types, paths between paths, type equivalence).

title: Visual Guide to Homotopy Type Theory

thesis: An eight-section canvas-based English-language visual guide to HoTT with more technical depth than its sibling hott.html: types as spaces (click to add points), paths as equalities (reflexivity, deformation), path operations (refl, inverse, composition, associativity up to 2-path), higher paths (2-path/homotopy animation), transport along paths (fibers, fibrations), the ladder of homotopy levels (contractible → proposition → set → groupoid → 2-groupoid), the circle S¹ with winding number π₁(S¹) ≃ ℤ, and univalence (step-by-step: types → equivalence → univalence).
key_claims: Types are spaces; elements are points; the identity type x = y is the type of paths from x to y; this is proof-relevant mathematics (different paths = different proofs).
Paths form a groupoid: identity (refl_x : x = x), inverse (p⁻¹ : y = x), composition (p·q : x = z); associativity (p·q)·r = p·(q·r) holds only up to a 2-path, making types ∞-groupoids.
A 2-path (homotopy) is a continuous deformation between two paths; p·p⁻¹ is not literally the constant path but there exists a 2-path deforming it to the constant one.
Transport: given a family of types P: A → Type and a path p: x = y, transport gives p_*: P(x) → P(y); this makes type families into fibrations over the base space.

Homotopy levels stratify types: (-2) contractible (one point), (-1) proposition (any two elements equal), (0) set (all paths between points equal), (1) groupoid (non-trivial paths, trivial 2-paths), (2) 2-groupoid (non-trivial 2-paths); every n-type is also an (n+1)-type.
The circle S¹ has one base point and one non-trivial loop; π₁(S¹) ≃ ℤ (winding number); the encode function transports 0 along the loop applying successor/predecessor.
Univalence: (A ≃ B) ≃ (A = B); two equivalent types can be identified; any theorem proven about A automatically applies to B — isomorphic structures share all properties for free.
